title: Proof Protocol
concept: Proof is a specific change, evidence you can both see, and a set time window. A promise without those is just hope.
whenToUse: After any real request for change; whenever “I promise” shows up with no actual plan; instead of just hoping things get better.
steps: Name the change — be specific and something you can actually observe.
Decide what counts — what does met, partial, and missed look like?
Set a time window — start date, end date, and when you’ll check in.
Record it simply — a count or a table — to see and review at the agreed check-in. At the check-in, feelings and questions come first; the record is an aid, never the judge.
Check in — extend it, adjust it, or close it out. Stay on the same team.
If it keeps getting missed without anyone owning it, that’s worth raising.

phrases.text: I need proof, not a promise. The change: ___. Evidence: ___. Window: ___. Check-in: ___.
I’m committing to ___, visible as ___, through ___.
At check-in: how are we each feeling? Then let’s look at the record together.

working: The change: every Pause + Return comes with an exact return time. Each return is noted, kept or not, and you see and review it together at the agreed check-in after 14 days. Six out of six kept, so trust moves forward.
notWorking: “I’ll be better at communicating.” No specific behaviour, no evidence, no time window. It feels good for a minute and changes nothing.
activity: Write one proof item today: the behaviour, the evidence, the time window, and when you’ll check in. Both of you sign off on it.
